subject: VPC egress path regression observed after control-plane upgrade — mitigation & runbook
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team <ops@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -0400
Subject: Visible failures after tonight's private control-plane upgrade

Hi Marcus / Evelyn,

We started seeing intermittent outbound connection failures from our private deployment shortly after your scheduled control-plane upgrade that ran ~02:00 UTC. Symptoms: several services in our VPC lost the ability to reach external tokenization endpoints (timeouts, TCP RSTs). The failures were isolated to instances using the egress NAT path — control-plane health on the nodes reported OK, but connections would hang for 10-30s before recovery.

We've collected basic traces and toggled the pod egress to our backup subnet which immediately reduced errors. More details attached (network-trace-20270316.pcap). Can you confirm whether any egress routing, security-group, or NAT gateway changes were included in the upgrade? This is causing transaction delays for a small percentage of requests and we'd like an ETA for a mitigation.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Sr. SRE, Cardinal Health
ops@cardinalhealth.com

Attachments: network-trace-20270316.pcap (pcap, 2.1MB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Visible failures after tonight's private control-plane upgrade

Hi Sofia — thank you for the report and the PCAP. We're looking into this now. Quick summary of next steps from our side: 

1) Immediate mitigation — we recommend keeping the traffic routed via your backup subnet until we confirm the root cause. If you'd like, Redwood can enact a temporary egress route pin (no config change on your side) to keep traffic off the affected path.
2) Investigation — our on-call infra team will correlate the control-plane rollout events (kernel module reloads, routing table reconcile) with the timestamps in your PCAP.
3) Postmortem & runbook — we'll share an initial incident timeline and a temporary runbook for recovery steps within 48 hours.

Can you confirm whether you want us to apply the temporary egress route pin now? If you prefer to keep your own workaround, we'll proceed with forensics first.

I'll open a tracking ticket (RED-4821) and attach the runbook draft when ready.

— Marcus

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Visible failures after tonight's private control-plane upgrade

Marcus — I reviewed the rollout logs from the night of 2027-03-16 and found that a change in the control-plane's NAT health-check ordering coincided with a short window where we flushed eBPF egress programs on a subset of hosts. That flush can transiently restore default routing for a few seconds while the new program compiles. In a saturated path this can lead to packet reordering or short stalls which look like 10-30s timeouts in your traces.

I recommend the following immediate steps (we've prepared a doc attached):
- Keep Cardinal traffic on the backup subnet (you already took this action which reduced errors)
- Redwood can push a near-term hotfix to avoid eBPF program flushes during the next reconcile — this is low-risk and we can roll in a canary within 4 hours if you approve
- We'll also provide a deterministic rollback of the control-plane change if the hotfix is not acceptable to you

Sofia — Marcus, Laura and I are available for a quick 30-minute bridge now if you'd like to go over options.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
evelyn@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_runbook_vpc-egress_v1.docx (runbook draft)

Subject: Follow-up & action items — VPC egress regression (postmortem preview)

Sofia — thanks again for working with us on this over the last 48 hours. Below is an interim summary and next steps; we'll publish a full postmortem and timeline in RED-4821 early next week.

Interim summary
- Incident window: 2027-03-16 01:58:00 UTC — 2027-03-16 03:04:00 UTC (control-plane rollout to primary egress hosts)
- Impact: Intermittent outbound TCP stalls observed by Cardinal Health services. ~0.8% of connections experienced >10s latency spikes, isolated to flows using the affected egress path.
- Root cause (preliminary): eBPF program flush during control-plane reconcile produced a transient default-route fallback on a subset of egress hosts; under load this introduced packet reordering and stalled flows.

Actions taken
- Cardinal rerouted egress traffic to backup subnet — immediate mitigation (customer action)
- Redwood prepared and validated hotfix to avoid eBPF flush during reconcile; canary-tested on internal cluster with no regression
- Created runbook for customers to pin egress path and for Redwood operators to perform safe reconciles (attached: redwood_runbook_vpc-egress_v1.docx)

Planned next steps
- Immediate: Coordinate scheduled hotfix canary with Cardinal ops during a 1-hour maintenance window. Proposed window: 2027-03-19 02:00–03:00 UTC. Please confirm availability.
- Short term: Publish full incident timeline, log artifacts, and telemetry in RED-4821.
- Long term: Add an automated pre-check to detect egress path saturation before reconcile and block eBPF flush if risk exists. ETA Q2 2027.

Attachments & links
- redwood_runbook_vpc-egress_v1.docx (attached)
- network-trace-20270316.pcap (provided by Cardinal)
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4821
- Runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cVPC-Runbook

Please let us know if you prefer we schedule the canary or if you'd like Redwood to perform the canary silently and only announce if we detect a regression. We're happy to follow the Cardinal change window or use our own maintenance window depending on your change control.
